extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and applicants filing ex parte appeals before the USPTO Board (appellants, patent attorneys/agents, examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive/formal requirements for filing and prosecuting ex parte appeals to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (now PTAB), including what must be in the appeal brief, timing/fees, admissibility of post-appeal amendments/evidence, and claim-specific explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The citation format used by parties before the Board must be consistent with Board practice. Primary authority should be cited for legal issues in papers directed to the Board; unless primary authority is unavailable, primary authority is always preferable to, and more persuasive than, any secondary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation to the MPEP is not barred but secondary authority is discouraged; rely on binding/primary authority where available; follow Board citation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee location and payment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for Board proceedings are located in part 41 (§ 41.20); some of the § 41.20 fees must be paid before jurisdiction passes to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees were moved to part 41 to group them with rules that require them; cross-references (e.g., § 1.17(b)) have been added to guide practitioners about where to pay and when payment affects jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal filing timing (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal (notice of appeal and accompanying fee) must be filed within the time period provided under § 1.134 for response to either a final rejection or a non-final rejection which rejects the claims a second time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant files an amendment within the § 1.134 period, the applicant may not file an appeal outside the time period provided under § 1.134; the applicant must await a new rejection before appealing in such situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ripeness after two rejections (removal of 'or finally')
rubrics_metrics.description: So long as the applicant has twice been denied a patent, an appeal may be filed; the alternative language 'or finally' is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal may be filed after the second rejection even if a 'final' rejection has not been entered; this aligns with Ex parte Lemoine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination appeal timing (patent owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexamination proceedings filed on or after November 29, 1999, a patent owner must wait until an examiner makes a second or subsequent rejection final before being permitted to file an appeal (per 35 U.S.C. 134(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections § 41.31(a)(2) and (a)(3) inform patent owners when appeals in reexamination may be taken; statutory requirements control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'date of filing' for appeal-related timing
rubrics_metrics.description: References to timing in Board rules use the 'date of filing the notice of appeal' rather than ambiguous phrases like 'date the proceeding has been appealed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date is either (1) date of deposit with USPS under 37 CFR § 1.10 or (2) date of receipt by the Office; this clarifies which date controls for various time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary admission of amendments/evidence after appeal ('may')
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of 'may' in § 41.33 indicates that entry of amendments and evidence filed after appeal is not a matter of right but may be admitted under certain circumstances set forth in the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission is discretionary and consistent with § 1.116 standards; examiners/Board have flexibility to admit or deny post-appeal filings as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-appeal amendments and evidence admission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments submitted on or after the date the proceeding has been appealed may be admitted as provided in § 1.116. Amendments filed on or after the date of filing a brief may be admitted only to cancel claims or to rewrite dependent claims into independent form (where cancellation does not affect scope of other pending claims), or otherwise only as permitted by §§ 41.39(b)(1), 41.50(a)(2)(i), 41.50(b)(1), and 41.50(c). Affidavits or other evidence submitted after appeal and prior to filing the brief may be admitted if the examiner determines they overcome all rejections under appeal and there is good and sufficient reason such evidence was not earlier presented; other affidavits/evidence after appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by specified provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final but prior to appeal, and amendments after appeal but prior to brief, are treated under § 1.116; stricter limitations apply after filing a brief. Good-and-sufficient-reason showings and examiner determinations are required for admission of certain affidavits/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees on subsequent appeals after prosecution reopened
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a Notice of Appeal and Appeal Brief fees have been paid in a proceeding, a second Notice of Appeal and Appeal Brief fee generally will not be required except if a final Board decision has been made on the first appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner reopens prosecution after fee payment, new fees are not required to appeal from that new Office action; if the Board makes a final decision on the first appeal and prosecution is later reopened, new fees are required for subsequent appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewriting dependent claims into independent form (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewriting dependent claims into independent form includes: (1) rewriting a dependent claim in independent form by adding thereto the limitations of the parent claim(s); and (2) rewriting an independent claim to incorporate therein all the subject matter of a dependent claim, canceling the dependent claim, and changing the dependency of claims that depended on the canceled dependent claim to the amended independent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP will provide guidance; these situations are permitted under § 41.33 when rewriting dependent claims into independent form is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of related proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellants must identify related proceedings, but this does not require identification of prior proceedings involving unrelated parties or every precedential decision that might bear on the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related proceedings include commonly owned applications having common subject matter or claims to a common priority application; listing unrelated precedential decisions is not required and could create unreasonable burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of status of all claims and identification of appealed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal brief must present a statement of the status of all the claims (e.g., rejected, allowed/confirmed, withdrawn, objected to, canceled) and identify which claims are being appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generally incorporates former § 1.192(c)(3) requirements; the Board uses this to determine scope of review and whether to make new grounds of rejection under § 41.50(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise explanation of subject matter of each independent claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each independent claim involved in the appeal must be provided, with reference to the specification by page and line number and to the drawing, if any, by reference characters; appellant may include any other information of record to aid the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is 'concise' is case-specific; the explanation need not show how each claim is different. The purpose is to aid claim construction and enable the Board to perform informed, claim-by-claim patentability determinations; appellant may decide whether to reference one representative drawing or multiple embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of means-plus-function / step-plus-function elements (35 U.S.C. 112(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every means-plus-function and step-plus-function limitation as permitted by 35 U.S.C. 112(6) used in the claims must be identified and the structure, material, or acts described in the specification as corresponding to each claimed function must be set forth with reference to the specification by page and line number and to the drawing, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies only to each independent claim involved in the appeal and to each dependent claim argued separately; concerns about estoppel are matters for proceedings outside the Office. Whether language invokes 112(6) is a merits issue discussed in MPEP 2181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim patentability and argumentation (waiver risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability must be decided on a claim-by-claim basis; arguments in the Appeal Brief are preferably directed to individual claims. If appellant groups claims, the Board will pick a single claim to decide the appeal for that group. Failure to separately argue claims that are grouped may constitute waiver of arguments for dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejections are 'jumbled' or unclear as to which grounds apply to which claims, appellant can seek relief via petition under § 1.181. The waiver provision reflects case law (e.g., In re McDaniel) that grouping claims can waive separate patentability arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed structure and information in appeal briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal Briefs must follow a prescribed format to ensure the Board has the information needed to render an informed decision; there is certain information common to each appeal that is amenable to prescribed format requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While appeals are unique, a set structure helps the Board; examiners' procedural requirements are found in the MPEP (e.g., MPEP 1208 for Examiner's Answer). The prescribed format is intended to reduce remands and improve clarity of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of 'separate' before 'patentability' (clarification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules were amended to add the word 'separate' prior to 'patentability' in § 41.37(c)(1)(vii) and § 41.67(c)(1)(vii) to clarify that pointing out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument for 'separate' patentability of a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that description of what a claim recites is not itself an argument that the claim is separately patentable; explicit argument is required for separate patentability positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal brief must include an evidence appendix containing copies of any evidence submitted to the examiner and relied upon by the appellant in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 41.7(b) was amended to allow this requirement to be consistent with the rule that precludes filing papers previously filed in the same Board proceeding without authorization; include copies of relied-upon evidence to permit Board review.
